reason: Table rows, footnote 1 (public AMI on or after July 15, 2023 means disabled even if now private) and the sentence on blocking and already-public AMIs together state every part of the claim.
The case study sentence says JPL will use On-Demand pricing with no long-term commitments and On-Demand Capacity Reservations for critical processing; the claim keeps the future tense.
The quote states that since most of the processing system is fault tolerant, JPL will take advantage of Spot Instances for scaling.
The document history row dated June 2, 2026 and the What's New post of Jun 10, 2026 both state cancelling a future-dated Capacity Reservation with a possible charge; the claim names both sources.
The Instance Types Guide document history rows give M9g/M9gd on June 9, C9g and C9gd on June 30 and R9g/R9gd on August 31, 2026, with Graviton5 for the M and R rows.
The Elastic IP pricing sentence and the blog table (in-use row no charge before Feb 1, 2024; secondary and idle Elastic IP already $0.005) support every part, with the in-use scope kept.

The Dedicated Host billing page lists the three reservation payment options with one-year and three-year terms, the three-year No Upfront limit, All Upfront lowest effective price, and Savings Plans with the u-6tb1 to u-24tb1 exclusion.
The FAQ answer states hibernate persists RAM, stop clears RAM, and in both cases EBS root and data volume data is persisted.
The FAQ states a typical time under 10 minutes from RunInstances to boot sequence and the three factors; the claim says typically and qualifier says not guaranteed.
The FAQ answer states the default private and public IP, the private IP staying across stop and start, and the public address lasting until stop, termination or replacement by an Elastic IP.
The FAQ answer and its two bullets give both conditions and the single charge per instance.
The FAQ sentence states EBS root data persists independently of instance lifetime and that this allows stop and restart.
The FAQ states no charge for the first hour when EC2 stops or terminates, nearest second when the user does, and the SLES entire-hour exception.
The FAQ answer 'No.' to being guaranteed, with the same availability and prices as a single Spot request.
The FAQ states a running Spot Instance can be stopped and kept, and that stop is available for persistent Spot requests; the claim attributes this to the FAQ without adding 'only'.

The quotes support 1152 vCPUs for Standard, 128 vCPUs for F, G, Inf, P and X, and that new accounts may start lower, but the qualifier condition states Service Quotas defaults of 5 for Standard and 0 for the other families, which no quote of this fact shows.
The pricing page states 100 GB free per month aggregated across services and Regions except China and GovCloud, and the aggregation sentence for rate tiers.
The FAQ says interpreted-language apps not reliant on native CPU instruction sets should run with minimal to no changes, and compiled-language apps need re-compiling for Arm.
The prerequisites page states the family rule, the bare metal exclusion, the four family lists with the named general purpose members, and all Regions.
The quotes give both IMDS addresses, the enable-and-use condition for IPv6, and the Nitro and IPv6-subnet requirement.
The quotes give the three precedence levels, separate evaluation of each option, and the AMI level applying only to HttpTokens and HttpPutResponseHopLimit.
Both sentences are quoted: multiple AZs protect from the failure of a single location, and you can design your application so another AZ's instance handles requests.
The quota table row shows default 0 and adjustable Yes for P instances, and the intro states per account per Region and vCPU units.
The quota row shows default 5 and adjustable Yes, and the intro sentence states per account per Region and vCPU management.
The pricing page states one-second increments, 60-second minimum, all purchase options, and lists the OSes in the condition.
The rules bullet states the 5 Gbps limit for internet and Direct Connect traffic for cluster placement groups, as the claim does.
Both quotes support single AZ, no spanning of multiple AZs, and spanning peered VPCs in the same Region.
The quotes state partitions in multiple AZs of a Region, visibility into partitions, and sharing with topology-aware applications such as HDFS, HBase and Cassandra.
The table row with its header gives Instance store, Compatibility Not applicable, and the Migrate to a new instance type instructions; the claim reports the table.

The table rows and the two examples are supported, but the claim drops the example's conditions: a default tenancy Amazon Linux/Unix Regional Reserved Instance, and instances in the same Region (US East (N. Virginia)); the claim states the benefit as holding for any t2.medium Reserved Instance.
The page says you can request a quota increase on receiving that error, and to use the Service Quotas console.
The row shows default 5 and adjustable Yes; the intro states per account per Region, vCPUs, and automatic adjustment.
The quotes state only EC2 can restart, persistent request restart in the same AZ and instance type, and the same launch specification condition.
The quotes state stop protection also protects from accidental termination, does not stop OS shutdown, and does not stop Auto Scaling termination when unhealthy or in scale-in.
